subline: 15 bench figures scored against the truth · 41 further chart candidates from 14 papers judged by eye · 18 Nov 2026
lede: On the 10 bench figures that hold data, the splitter finds 32 of the 33 charts on its own and all 33 once it is told how many charts a figure holds; the round-1 splitter found 20. Those are the figures it was built on. On 30 further data figures from the same papers, with no truth and judged by eye, it cuts 7 cleanly, 4 with a title or legend in the wrong box, and 19 wrongly.
scorednote: The one miss is C4: its two charts stay in one box, because one of them offers only two tick labels the splitter can use and it asks for three. The rule still counts one of the two as found, since the single box overlaps it by 0.50. Told that the figure holds two charts, the splitter cuts them, with an overlap of 0.97. Round 2 reported 33 of 33: that was the local method, which gets the count from the model's first call. The prepared folders that the cloud and agent methods read are cut without a model and hold C4 as one chart. C3's third box overlaps its truth box by only 0.53 because it also holds the legend beside the chart.
modenote: Charts found by the bench's rule, out of 33. The round-1 splitter cuts at white gutters at least 1 % of the image wide. The splitter first looks for runs of three or more tick labels and cuts between the charts they mark, then falls back to gutters. With the chart count, an axis of only two tick labels is accepted when it gives exactly that many charts; here the truth's count stands in for the model's.
widenote: Every other figure the conversion typed as a chart in the 23 converted papers: 41 figures from 14 papers, the bench's 15 left out. Nobody has drawn truth boxes for these, so there is no score. The tables say what the splitter did, the pictures show it, and each card says what a look by eye found. 11 of the 41 are not charts at all (diagrams, screenshots, a logo, a crop of body text that the figure typer let through); the reading methods decline such figures, so their boxes do not matter.
widelook: The verdicts were given once, by eye, by the model that built this page, from pictures like the ones below. They are a first reading, not a measurement: check any that matter to you. The boxes drawn are the splitter's own, as the prepare step stores them.
findings: Charts that share their tick labels are merged

Grids that print tick labels once per row or column give the splitter too few axes. AMIE-Mx pictures_8: 15 line charts come out as 5 column boxes. AMIE-Mx pictures_5: 20 bar charts come out as 17 boxes of the wrong widths. Med-RwR pictures_7: six charts in three row boxes. Zodiac pictures_4 and pictures_12: heatmaps that share row labels stay in one box.
Numbers in or beside a chart are taken for tick labels

The values printed in heatmap cells, and the ticks of a colour bar, line up like an axis. Dynamic-Specialist-MAS pictures_2: one heatmap cut in two. Wang pictures_3: a heatmap cut in three, one piece joined to the ring chart beside it. RiskAgent pictures_1: every colour bar becomes a box, and one chart is cut in half beside its colour bar.
An axis is cut away from its chart

EchoAgent-EHM pictures_2: the x axis of a bar chart is a box of its own. AMIE-Mx pictures_4: two strips of x labels are boxes. RiskAgent pictures_6: four charts with a second y axis lose their left axis labels.
Composites under panel letters are barely split

Figures that mix chart types under letters a, b, c. Wang pictures_1: six panels, two boxes. Wang pictures_2: five panels, two boxes. Med-RwR pictures_2: three charts, two boxes. AgentMD pictures_3: two panels, one box.
Some charts end up in no box

AgentMD pictures_8: three of eight small density charts. HeartAgent pictures_2: part of the six small stacked-bar charts. AMIE-Mx pictures_5: charts of the bottom row. A reader that is sent only the boxes never sees these.
Titles and legends land in the wrong box

AMIE-Cardiology pictures_5, HeartAgent pictures_3, RiskAgent pictures_5, AgentMD pictures_7. The charts are separated; a title, an axis title or a legend sits in the neighbour's box or outside every box. The values are unaffected, the names may not be.

Grids where every chart prints its own tick labels or stands apart by a clear gutter. HeartAgent pictures_1: 12 of 12. HeartAgent pictures_4: 4 of 4. AgentMD pictures_5: 3 of 3. EchoAgent-EHM pictures_3 and AMIE-Mx pictures_16: 2 of 2. And the bench figures, which it was built on.
Three figures could not be prepared at all

CardAIc-Agents pictures_2 and pictures_3, and Risk-Score-Interfaces Supplementary pictures_1: the prepare step failed while writing their printed text (characters from the PDF that cannot be encoded as UTF-8). They are not among the 41. That is a defect of the prepare step, not of the splitter.
limits: A chart is found by a run of three or more numbers that are aligned and evenly spaced. Pies, and charts without numeric ticks, fall back to white gutters (round 2). Seen here on Med-RwR pictures_3: two pies left as one.
A second y axis cuts a chart
Predicted in round 2 and seen here on RiskAgent pictures_6: the labels of the left axis are cut away from all four charts.
It was built on ten figures

The rules were written while looking at the bench's ten data figures. 32 of 33 charts there against 7 of 30 figures cut cleanly here is the size of that effect. The two numbers are not the same measure: one counts charts against truth boxes, the other counts whole figures by eye.

The local method sends the model one box at a time, so a wrong cut loses or merges charts for it. The cloud and agent methods also get the whole figure and are told the boxes can be wrong; on the bench they returned every value. A wrong cut still hands them misleading crops and chart ids.
Eleven of 41 candidates are not charts

That is the figure typer upstream, not the splitter. The splitter still draws boxes on them (five on a journal logo), which wastes nothing but the prepare time: the readers decline such figures at their first step.
